title: Wilbur and Orville Wright: The First Airplane

source.name: VOA Learning English — Wilbur and Orville Wright: The First Airplane
source.license: Nội dung của VOA (Voice of America), phạm vi công cộng
source.note: Đã rút gọn: chỉ giữ một số đoạn.

paras: Wilbur and Orville Wright are the American inventors who made a small engine-powered flying machine. They proved that flight without the aid of gas-filled balloons was possible.
Wilbur Wright was born in 1867 near Melville, Indiana. His brother Orville was born four years later in Dayton, Ohio.

As they grew up, the Wright brothers experimented with mechanical things. Later, the Wright brothers began to design their own flying machine. They used ideas they had developed from earlier experiments with a toy helicopter, kites, the printing machine and bicycles.

Soon, they needed a place to test their ideas about flight. The best place with the best wind conditions seemed to be a piece of sandy land in North Carolina along the coast of the Atlantic Ocean. It was called Kill Devil Hill, near the town of Kitty Hawk.
The Wright brothers did many tests with gliders at Kitty Hawk. With these tests, they learned how to solve many problems.
By the autumn of 1903, Wilbur and Orville had designed and built an airplane powered by a gasoline engine. The plane had wings 12 meters across. It weighed about 340 kilograms, including the pilot.

On December 17th, 1903, they made the world's first flight in a machine that was heavier than air and powered by an engine. Orville flew the plane 36 meters. He was in the air for 12 seconds. The two brothers made three more flights that day.
Four other men watched the Wright brothers' first flights. One of the men took pictures. Few newspapers, however, noted the event.

It was almost five years before the Wright brothers became famous. In 1908, Wilbur went to France. He gave demonstration flights at heights of 90 meters. A French company agreed to begin making the Wright brothers' flying machine.

Orville made successful flights in the United States at the time Wilbur was in France. The United States War Department agreed to buy a Wright brothers' plane. Wilbur and Orville suddenly became world heroes. But the brothers were not seeking fame. They returned to Dayton where they continued to improve their airplanes. They taught many others how to fly.
Wilbur Wright died of typhoid fever in 1912. Orville Wright continued designing and inventing until he died many years later, in 1948.

Today, the Wright brothers' first airplane is in the Air and Space Museum in Washington, D.C. Visitors to the museum can look at the Wright brothers' small plane. Then they can walk to another area and see space vehicles and a rock collected from the moon. The world has changed a lot since Wilbur and Orville Wright began the modern age of flight over one hundred years ago.

questions.q: What did the Wright brothers show through their invention?
options: Powered flight was possible without gas-filled balloons
An engine could be built entirely from bicycle parts
Balloons were safer than any machine that has an engine
Gliders could carry more passengers than aeroplanes could
questions.explain: Đoạn 1: họ “proved that flight without the aid of gas-filled balloons was possible”.

questions.q: Where did the brothers’ ideas for their flying machine come from?
options: They were copied from plans supplied by a French company
They were taken from the books of earlier inventors of the aeroplane
They came from watching birds fly along the Atlantic coast
They grew out of earlier work with toys and everyday machines
questions.explain: Đoạn 3: họ dùng ý tưởng từ các thí nghiệm trước với trực thăng đồ chơi, diều, máy in và xe đạp.

questions.q: Why did the brothers choose a stretch of sandy coast for their tests?
options: It was close to their family home and workshop in the state of Ohio
Many newspaper reporters lived in the villages that were nearby
The winds there suited their experiments better than other places
The soft sand made crash landings much less dangerous for the pilot
questions.explain: Đoạn 4: “The best place with the best wind conditions seemed to be a piece of sandy land in North Carolina”. Bài không nói cát giúp đáp xuống an toàn.

questions.q: How did the world react to the first flights in December 1903?
options: Crowds of reporters travelled to the coast to describe the event at length
Few people noticed, since only a handful saw them and few papers reported them
Several photographers sold pictures of the flights to the big magazines
The government decided at once to buy the aeroplane for its army
questions.explain: Đoạn 8: chỉ bốn người chứng kiến, một người chụp ảnh và “Few newspapers, however, noted the event”.

options: Public flights abroad and at home, about five years after the first one
Newspaper reports that appeared on the day after their very first flight
A race in which their aeroplane beat a gas-filled balloon over the sea
A prize that the War Department awarded to them in the year 1903
questions.explain: Đoạn 9–10: gần năm năm sau mới nổi tiếng; năm 1908 Wilbur bay biểu diễn ở Pháp, Orville bay thành công ở Mỹ và Bộ Chiến tranh đồng ý mua máy bay.

questions.q: What does the writer suggest about the brothers’ attitude to fame?
options: They enjoyed being world heroes and travelled widely to meet fans
They hoped to become rich by selling their planes to governments
Improving their planes and teaching others mattered more to them
They wanted to keep their ideas secret from other inventors
questions.explain: Đoạn 10: “the brothers were not seeking fame. They returned to Dayton where they continued to improve their airplanes. They taught many others how to fly.”

questions.q: Wilbur and Orville Wright were born in different towns.
questions.explain: Đoạn 2: Wilbur sinh gần Melville, bang Indiana; Orville sinh ở Dayton, bang Ohio.

questions.q: The brothers’ first aeroplane was badly damaged in a crash soon after its first flights.
questions.explain: Bài không nói máy bay bị hỏng hay rơi sau những chuyến bay đầu tiên.
